verdict: Below threshold (5.0 < 7.5): not ready for a top-conference submission. The manuscript is an unusually honest, carefully hedged, pre-registered characterisation study, but its contributions are narrow (one cell per regime, planar simulation, three seeds, mostly null or exploratory learning results), and the draft still contains unfinished content (a [PENDING] random row and a placeholder Figure 1). Its main positive finding (small one-step headroom) is expected from theory and is bounded only over 32 screened actions with a reduced completion. The most transferable observation (the g_T versus grid-posterior ordering inversion) rests on point estimates in one cell, with no interval.
strengths: Rigorous pre-registration discipline: frozen hypotheses, gates, outcome map and an amendment before S2. Failed gates (D3 twice, D4) are reported plainly, and exploratory rows are clearly separated from registered ones.

Validated headroom estimator: notch and travel-notch constructions with known exact gaps, a zero-gap false-positive bank and an on-belief bias check, plus an explicit statement that G is one-step-deviation headroom, not the gap to the optimal policy.
Controlled learner comparison: the same belief-free DeepSets head, action set and feasibility mask for DAgger distillation and PPO, so the training signal is the isolated variable.
The g_T (sPCE-type) versus posterior ordering disagreement is a potentially useful methodological warning for amortized experimental-design work that reports contrastive bounds as policy quality.

Careful behavioural diagnostics: the travel decomposition separates the grid snap from between-probe travel, and the probe counts, zero-move fractions and per-seed travel correlations show what each policy actually does in each regime.

Honest cost analysis: the latency decomposition explains why candidate pruning cannot reach the 10x target, and reduced-size planners are compared against the students, which is the fair alternative to amortization.
The limitations section is thorough, and nearly every quantitative claim carries a paired crossed-bootstrap ci95 and a statement of its evidential status.
weaknesses: Unfinished manuscript: the S2 random test row is still [PENDING:...] in Table 2, Table 5 and Section 7, and Figure 1 is an explicit placeholder. Either alone blocks submission.

Thin empirical scope: one cell per regime, one planar shape library (K = 8), simulated Gaussian sensing with no contact dynamics, no held-out shapes, no 3D objects and no hardware. Every regime-dependent claim is an untested two-cell comparison.

Low statistical power: three seeds per learner make H2 and H2-S2 sensitive only to advantages of about 0.5 nats. No equivalence test was run, there is no multiplicity correction, and the test split was reused by all S2 rows, E5, B-fan and the long student.

The headline result H3 (Hold) is close to what adaptive-submodularity arguments predict, and it covers only 32 mostly random screened first actions with a reduced greedy completion. The upward selection bias of V_LA was not measured, and there is no full 512-action screen or structured travel-then-fan family. Its novelty and informativeness are limited.

The learning results are mostly negative or unresolved: no learner reaches G*, H2 is not detected in either cell, and the belief-input control is under-fit and isolates nothing. As a result the paper yields few actionable conclusions.

The RL comparator is weak and untuned for S2: it uses a single configuration selected at the edge of the learning-rate grid, and all six PPO policies collapse to exactly three probes. This undermines H2 and H2-S2 as a comparison of distillation against RL in general.

The g_T/posterior inversion, the most transferable claim, has no interval for g_T(G*) - g_T(learner) in either cell. It is marginal in S12, near-cap compression was not measured on test, and it is confounded with RL's fixed three-probe behaviour.

The evaluator is not shown to have converged: gate E' failed, no sub-16 check was run, and the 7.5 % success flip rate between subdivisions is of the same order as most success contrasts, including the S2 student versus B-fan +8.1 pp.

The S2 validation/test discrepancy is unexplained (about 2 combined SE, wider for every seed). The S2 training record shows over-fitting under the registered last-checkpoint recipe, which weakens the S2 learnability conclusion as a statement about distillation rather than about this recipe.

Baselines in S2 are incomplete: only B-fan (the S12 H*) was run. The S2 separation is therefore from a stay-and-fan heuristic that is mismatched to a travelling regime, not from the best available heuristic.
S2 Cal' verification was done after the experiments, and the E5 latencies are logged medians on free runners rather than Lat' measurements.

Presentation: the text is dense with qualifiers, derived figures and parenthetical caveats, which obscures a clear take-home message. Several numbers are repeated across the abstract, introduction, results and conclusion with slightly different splits.
required_actions: Complete the S2 random test3 row and remove every [PENDING] marker. Produce Figure 1, or remove the reference to it.

Add more cells per regime (several kappa values and at least one more shape library) and more learner seeds (at least 5 to 10), so that regime-dependent claims can be tested across cells rather than stated anecdotally.

Compute bootstrap intervals for g_T(G*) - g_T(learner) in both cells, measure near-cap compression of g_T on test, and run a probe-count-aware or S2-tuned RL variant so that the g_T/posterior inversion can be separated from RL's three-probe collapse.

Strengthen H3: run a full 512-action first-step screen and a structured travel-then-fan candidate family, measure the selection bias of V_LA (for example with an independent re-estimate of the selected action), and ideally add a two-step look-ahead estimate.
Validate the evaluator at a finer grid (sub-16) on set S, or report success contrasts with the evaluator's resolution folded into the uncertainty.
Use a fresh, untouched test split for the S2 rows and the student versus B-fan claims, or confine those claims explicitly to exploratory status in the abstract.
Investigate the S2 validation/test gap with more episodes and seeds, and test early stopping on held-out regret as a pre-declared sensitivity analysis.
Run B-spread and B-cov (or select an S2 H* on S2 pilot data) so that the travelling-regime comparison is against the best available heuristic.
Fit a working belief-input or attention-based head so that the representation question can be answered, and measure regret on student-visited states to test the covariate-shift explanation.
Time the reduced planners and the students under the Lat' protocol and plot a latency-accuracy frontier.
Tighten the writing: state one clear take-home message per contribution, move derived and post-hoc sensitivity figures to an appendix, and remove repeated numbers across sections.
